title: plugin-audit: `activityMilestones` summary templates still interpolate raw lookup ids — `{owner_id}` renders `oBK25…` after #7230
body:
Found while implementing #7230 (`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-writers.ts`). Filed rather than fixed — the fix has a hot-path cost that #7230's shape deliberately avoids, so it needs its own decision.

## Mechanism

`matchMilestone` (ADR-0052 §5b.2) interpolates `{token}` in an author-written milestone summary from the after-row:

```ts
const summary = m.summary.replace(/\{(\w+)\}/g, (_match, key) => {
  const v = after[key];
  if (v === null || v === undefined || v === '') return '';
  const field = fields ? fields[key] : undefined;
  return field ? displayFieldValue(field, v) : String(v);
});
```

`displayFieldValue` is called with **no title map**, so a `lookup` / `master_detail` / `user` token falls through to `String(value)` — the raw id. A milestone declared as

```ts
activityMilestones: [{ field: 'stage', value: 'closed_won', summary: 'Deal won by {owner}' }]
```

renders `Deal won by oBK25…`.

The milestone branch takes **precedence** over the tracked-change branch #7230 fixed, so on objects that declare milestones this is the string users actually see.

## Why #7230 did not fix it

#7230 resolves reference titles from a read plan built off the **diff**, and only after `matchMilestone` has declined — so a write that moves no tracked reference field issues no read at all. That gate is what keeps #6656 / PR #6977's retirement of the redundant pre-image read (2 → 1 per single-id write, 3 → 0 per predicate write) from being handed back.

Resolving milestone tokens cannot reuse that gate. The tokens are read from the whole after-row, and whether a milestone fires is only known *after* `matchMilestone` runs, so the read would have to happen either:

- **before** `matchMilestone`, on every update of a milestone-declaring object — including the majority where no milestone fires and the read is wasted; or
- **after** it fires, keyed on the tokens that actually appear in the matched template — one read per distinct target object, paid only on the transition. Cheaper, and the transition is by construction rare (`before !== value && after === value`), but it needs `matchMilestone` to become async.

The second looks right, and is the one worth costing out. Either way the trade belongs to the maintainer, not to #7230's implementer.

Anchors at `a768f81a1` (pre-#7230): `matchMilestone` `audit-writers.ts:355`, the interpolation `:368-375`, its call site `:872`.

Refs: #7230, #6656 / PR #6977, ADR-0052 §5b.2.
